title: Ask for review of a real estate assessment and appeal to the Board of Equalization
question: I think my Charlottesville real estate assessment is too high. How do I ask for a review and appeal it, and what are the deadlines?
summary: Charlottesville assesses all real estate every year at fair market value as of January 1, and the city says change notices are mailed at the end of January. To contest a value, call the City Assessor's Office, then file a written Assessment Appeal Application, one per parcel, with evidence by the date printed on that year's notice and form (March 4 in 2026; February 28 in 2025). The review is free. The Assessor's review can lower, raise or keep the value, and the city says the decision is mailed within 30 days. If you disagree, appeal to the Board of Equalization within 30 days of that decision letter; the Board holds a hearing and mails its decision within 30 days. The last step is the Charlottesville Circuit Court, which has filing deadlines and court costs.

legal_basis.citation: City Code ch. 30, art. III (Real Estate Assessments)

steps.step: The City Assessor mails a notice of change in assessment
steps.how: Every parcel is assessed each year at fair market value as of January 1. The notice shows the new and prior two years' values and tax figures, and on its reverse the deadlines for asking the Assessor for a review and for appealing to the Board of Equalization. State law requires those deadlines to be stated on the notice.
steps.deadline: The city's FAQ says notices are mailed at the end of January; state law requires mailing at least 15 days before the hearing on objections (Va. Code § 58.1-3330(A))
steps.quote: Change of assessment notices are mailed annually at the end of January.

steps.step: Optional: talk to the appraiser who valued the property
steps.who: Property owner or authorized agent; the City Assessor's Office appraiser
steps.how: Call the City Assessor's Office (open by appointment only, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.) and give the owner name, the property address or the nine-digit parcel ID. The city says this call often clears up questions; a formal review needs the written application in the next steps.
steps.quote: The first step is to contact the City Assessor's Office at 434.970.3136 to speak with the appraiser who conducted the assessment of the property.

steps.step: Optional: inspect the assessment records for the property
steps.who: Property owner or authorized agent; City Assessor's Office
steps.how: Ask the office to see the property appraisal card and working papers, the methodology and comparable sales used, and a written explanation of any increase. Parcel records are also on the city's GIS Viewer.
steps.deadline: Appraisal cards are open for inspection after the reassessment notice is mailed (Va. Code § 58.1-3331(A))
steps.quote: the assessing officer shall provide a written explanation or justification for an increase in the property's assessed value.

steps.step: Prepare the Assessment Appeal Application and the evidence
steps.who: Property owner, or an agent with a Letter of Authorization
steps.how: Fill in the Assessment Appeal Application, one for each parcel. Give your proposed land, building and total values, explain why the value is wrong and attach supporting documentation showing that it (1) exceeds market value, (2) is substantially out of line with similar properties in the neighborhood, or (3) rests on factual errors such as square footage, acreage or condition. The 2026 form asks for up to three sales from the year before, or up to three comparable assessments. An agent must attach an original Letter of Authorization from the owner, signed before the application date and either notarized or on the owner's commercial letterhead (2026 form). Appeals on income-producing property must include the two most recent annual income and expense surveys and the current rent roll (2026 form). The city says the tax impact or the size of the change is not, by itself, grounds for an appeal.
steps.quote: Appeals should be made in writing, including the City’s Assessment Appeal Application, a Letter of Authorization if the appeal is being made by an owner’s agent, and any other supporting documentation that is appropriate.

steps.step: File the application with the City Assessor by the date on the notice
steps.how: Submit the form online from the Assessment Appeal Application Form page, or fill in the fillable PDF (the 2026 edition is in the city's Document Center) and either email it to the City Assessor's Office at the address given on the form page or mail it to City Assessor's Office, 102 5th Street NE, P.O. Box 911, Charlottesville, VA 22902. If you cannot download it, call the office; the City Assessor page says the office will mail you a hard copy.
steps.deadline: By the date printed on that year's notice and application form: on or before March 4, 2026 for the 2026 assessment (the city's 2025 sample notice gave February 28, 2025)
steps.fee: No fee or charge (2025 sample notice)
steps.quote: APPLICATION MUST BE FILED ON OR BEFORE MARCH 04, 2026

steps.step: The Assessor reviews the value and mails a decision
steps.who: City Assessor's Office (the appraiser who valued the property)
steps.how: The appraiser who valued the property meets with you to review the value, may inspect the property, and decides what change, if any, is appropriate. The 2026 form says the review ends with the assessment lowered, increased or not changed. If you accept the decision, nothing more is needed.
steps.deadline: Decision mailed within 30 days (Assessment Appeal Application Form page)
steps.quote: Notice of his decision will be provided to you within 30 days by mail.

steps.step: If you disagree, appeal to the Board of Equalization
steps.who: Property owner or authorized agent; Board of Equalization (appointed by the Judge of the Circuit Court)
steps.how: File the Board of Equalization appeal form. It is not posted online. The city's FAQ says Board hearings are scheduled after the City Assessor's Office receives the owner's request for further review, so ask that office for the form. Under state law a residential application cannot be refused for lack of information if it gives the address, the parcel number and your proposed value. A mailed paper form counts as received on its postmark date. State law lets the Board consider income and expense statements and sales through December 31 if they reach the Board by the locality's application deadline.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of the date of the Assessor's formal appeal decision letter
steps.quote: An appeal form for the Board must be filed within 30 days of the date of the formal appeal decision letter.

steps.step: Get the Assessor's records before the Board hearing (homes with fewer than four units)
steps.how: For a residential property with fewer than four units, the Assessor must mail a notice at least 45 days before the hearing that explains your right to the assessment records and to ask for a physical inspection. Ask for the records in writing. If the Assessor does not provide them, it must present its records and appraisal testimony before you present your case.
steps.deadline: Assessor must provide the records within 15 days of a written request
steps.quote: The assessing officer shall provide such records within 15 days of a written request by the taxpayer or his duly authorized representative.

steps.step: Present your case at the Board of Equalization hearing
steps.who: Board of Equalization; property owner or agent; City Assessor
steps.how: State law requires public notice of each Board sitting in a newspaper at least seven days ahead, and the city's 2025 notice says all hearings are open to the public. The Board presumes the Assessor's value is correct. You must show by a preponderance of the evidence that the value is above fair market value, or not uniform, and was not reached by accepted appraisal practice. The Board can raise a value as well as lower it. The 2025 sample notice scheduled the Board's sittings for May 13 to 15, 2025.
steps.deadline: The city's FAQ says hearings are scheduled within 30 days after the City Assessor's Office receives the request
steps.quote: A hearing will be scheduled to weigh the evidence that demonstrates that the property’s value is inconsistent with similar properties, is assessed above or below fair market value, or is inconsistent with the physical features of the property.

steps.how: The Board orders the assessment increased, decreased or affirmed and sends the order to the owner. If the value is lowered after the tax was paid, the owner is entitled to a refund of the excess.
steps.quote: Following their hearing and review of the appeal packet, the BOE will provide the property owner with their decision by mail within 30 days.

steps.step: If you still disagree, apply to the Charlottesville Circuit Court
steps.who: Property owner (taxpayer); Charlottesville Circuit Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: File an application to correct an erroneous assessment in the Clerk's Office, 315 East High Street, with the Cover Sheet for Filing Civil Actions (check Taxes, Correct Erroneous State/Local). Name the City of Charlottesville as a party. The court presumes the Assessor's or Board's value is correct, and the owner pays the court costs.
steps.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3984(A), 58.1-3382)
steps.fee: Court costs (amount not stated by the city; see fees)
steps.quote: (a) within three years from the last day of the tax year for which any such assessment is made, (b) within one year from the date of the assessment

steps.how: The case is heard by a judge without a jury. The court may lower the value to fair market value; if it finds the value below fair market value, it must raise it and order the proper taxes paid. If the tax was paid on an erroneous assessment, the court must order a refund with interest. The clerk certifies the change to the Commissioner of the Revenue and the Treasurer.
steps.quote: the court may reduce the assessment to what in its opinion based on the evidence is the fair market value of the property involved.

steps.step: Keep paying the real estate tax on the regular due dates
steps.how: The city's pages do not say that an appeal postpones the due dates. Late payments get a 10% penalty and interest. If the Board or the court later lowers the value, state law gives an exoneration or a refund (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3385, 58.1-3987).
steps.deadline: June 5 and December 5 each year (moved to the next Monday if the date falls on a weekend)
steps.quote: Real estate taxes are due in equal installments on June 5th and December 5th of each year.

escalation.trigger: Disagree with the City Assessor's review decision
escalation.next: Board of Equalization (appointed by the Charlottesville Circuit Court)
escalation.deadline: Within 30 days of the date of the formal appeal decision letter (city); a local date no earlier than 30 days after the Assessor's objection period ends (state floor, Va. Code § 58.1-3378)
escalation.quote: Any taxpayer or his duly appointed representative may apply to the board of equalization for the adjustment to fair market value and equalization of his assessment, including errors in acreage

escalation.trigger: No Assessor decision before the Board's filing deadline passes, or before the Board's term ends (the statutes speak of an application to the commissioner of the revenue or other official performing those duties; treating the City Assessor as that official is an inference)
escalation.next: Charlottesville Circuit Court, which may require the Board of Equalization (or reappoint it) to hear the appeal
escalation.deadline: The review must have been filed with the Assessor before the Board's deadline or the end of its term, and the taxpayer must tell the circuit court that he wishes to appeal to the Board. Reappointment under § 58.1-3370(B) applies only to a board appointed under that section
escalation.quote: then the circuit court may require the board of equalization to hear and act on such appeal.

escalation.trigger: Disagree with the Board of Equalization's order
escalation.deadline: Same time limit as Va. Code § 58.1-3984: three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the assessment, whichever is later
escalation.quote: may apply to the circuit court of the county or city, for the correction and revision of such order, in the same manner and within the same time as is provided by law for the correction of erroneous assessments of real estate by any person who is aggrieved thereby.

escalation.trigger: Assessor review denied and the owner goes to court without the Board. Unconfirmed for Charlottesville: state law allows this only where the Board is not a prerequisite to the court's jurisdiction, and the city's 2025 notice describes court after a Board hearing. Confirm with the Circuit Court Clerk's Office or a lawyer before skipping the Board
escalation.deadline: Three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the assessment, whichever is later
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made.

escalation.trigger: Disagree with the Circuit Court's final judgment
escalation.deadline: Notice of appeal within 30 days of the final judgment order
escalation.quote: a notice of appeal to the Court of Appeals in any case within the jurisdiction of the court shall be filed within 30 days from the date of any final judgment order, decree, or conviction.

caveats: Assessor review deadline: the 2026 Assessment Appeal Application gives March 4, 2026, so the 2026 window had closed by 2026-10-11. The 2025 sample notice gave February 28, 2025. The date changes from year to year and is printed on each year's notice and form; no 2027 date was published. The FAQ's statement that notices are mailed at the end of January is not confirmed from a 2026 notice.

Forms: the Assessment Appeal Application Form page describes an online form and a fillable PDF but links neither (as of 2026-10-11). The 2026 fillable PDF is in the city's Document Center (DocumentCenter/View/13021) and is recorded as form f1; next year's edition will probably have a new link. The online form was not found, and the FormCenter 'City Assessor' category lists no forms. The Board of Equalization appeal form is not posted online. The FAQ says Board hearings are scheduled after the City Assessor's Office receives the request for further review, so that office appears to supply and receive the form (confirm with the office).

The city's own statements differ. The City Assessor page says the Board appeal form is due within 30 days of the Assessor's decision letter. The sample notice says 'within 30 days after the ruling'. The FAQ instead says Board hearings are scheduled within 30 days after the Assessor's Office receives the request. The City Assessor page gives no time for the Assessor's decision, while the appeal form page and the FAQ say 30 days. The pages also number the steps differently.

Court route: the 2025 sample notice says an aggrieved person may apply to the Circuit Court 'after a hearing before the Board'. Va. Code §§ 58.1-3350 and 58.1-3984(A) allow a direct court application where the Board is not a prerequisite. Whether Charlottesville's code makes the Board a prerequisite was not determined.

Local ordinance not checked: the City Assessor FAQ cites the City Code (Chapter 30, Article III, Real Estate Assessments) on Municode. Municode's terms of use page answered HTTP 520 on 2026-10-10, and its library needs an authenticated API, so no Municode text is quoted. So the ordinance that sets the Board filing date under Va. Code § 58.1-3378, any rule on Board deadlines, and whether the Board is a permanent board under § 58.1-3373 or one appointed each year under § 58.1-3370 are all unconfirmed. Whether a city charter provision or a special act continued by § 58.1-3260 changes any step is also not confirmed.

Fees: the city says only that the owner pays 'all associated court costs'. Which Va. Code § 17.1-275 category the Clerk uses for a § 58.1-3984 application was not confirmed: (A)(26), $60 for civil actions without a money-damages claim, or (A)(13), $100 to $300 by amount sought. Other costs may apply: the $10 legal aid fee (§ 17.1-278) where it applies, local courthouse (up to $2, § 17.1-281) and law library (up to $4, § 42.1-70) assessments if the city adopted them, and service of process fees. The courts' Circuit Court Civil Filing Fee Calculation tool (https://www.vacourts.gov/ccfees_calc_app) was not used, because it is an interactive form.

No fee was found for a Board of Equalization appeal. The index holds no state fee for it, and the sample notice's 'No fee or charge' sentence appears under the City Assessor review heading, not the Board heading.

Paying tax during an appeal: the city's pages do not say whether an appeal postpones the June 5 and December 5 due dates. Va. Code § 58.1-3958 pauses collection only during an administrative appeal under § 58.1-3980 filed within 90 days of the assessment. Section 58.1-3980 reaches real estate only for errors by the assessing official, or factual errors in a general reassessment. Whether a Charlottesville Assessor review counts was not confirmed.

Risk of an increase: the 2026 application form says the Assessor's review itself can end in '(1) assessment lowered, (2) assessment increased or (3) assessment not changed'. The Board can increase as well as decrease an assessment (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3379(A), 58.1-3381(A)), and the court must raise one it finds below fair market value (§ 58.1-3987).

Agents: the 2026 form requires an original Letter of Authorization from the owner, signed before the application date and either notarized or on the owner's commercial letterhead. No template was found. Va. Code § 58.1-3380 presumes a notarized letter from the owner to be a valid designation before the Board. The 2025 notice says the 'property owner or lessee may file an appeal', but the 2026 form says the applicant must be the legal owner or a duly authorized agent; whether a lessee may file in Charlottesville was not confirmed.

Income-producing property: the Assessor may require income and expense statements (Va. Code § 58.1-3294), and failing to furnish them bars their use in court. The 2026 form requires the two most recent annual income and expense surveys and the current rent roll with appeals on income-producing property. The city's Income & Expense Forms page still asks (as of 2026-10-11) for the forms by October 3, 2023 for the 2024 reassessment, so its dates are out of date.

Court of Appeals: only the statutory route and the 30-day notice of appeal (Va. Code § 8.01-675.3) are recorded. The Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia (Part 5A) and the appeal fees are not covered here.

Dates and figures from the 2025 sample notice (the February 28 deadline and the Board sittings scheduled for May 13 to 15) are examples for 2025 only. The notice also cites the Board statute as 'Section 58-1.3378', a misprint for § 58.1-3378.

Privacy: the City Assessor pages publish a named staff mailbox for emailed appeals and name the Assessor, the sample notice is signed by a named official, the Real Estate Taxes page names the Treasurer, and the court page names the Clerk and judges. None of these is recorded; the email route is described by reference to the form page.

State-law quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia (none of these sections carries an effective-until date). They include that copy's spacing before punctuation after cross-references (for example '§ 58.1-3330 .'). The text has not been compared with law.lis.virginia.gov.
Cover sheet: form CC-1416 lists 'Taxes' with 'Correct Erroneous State/Local' (code CTAX). The court rule that calls for a cover sheet with a new civil filing was not read.

The online Assessment Appeal Application link and the Board of Equalization appeal form were not found online.
